definition: predict_pool's link term per RPC worker: rtt_trips x RTT + (hidden state out + its output back) / bandwidth, per decoded token and per prompt batch, with rtt_trips = 1 (was 2).

evidence.code: llama.cpp b23701f7 ggml/src/ggml-rpc/ggml-rpc.cpp:945-1047: SET_TENSOR and GRAPH_COMPUTE are sent one-way (send_async, no reply); only GET_TENSOR waits. Per worker visit: the request and the reply each cross the link once, so one round trip, plus the transfers.
evidence.measured: the network study (testbed/results/netshape_20261008_182208/score.json, NS-RTT): decode rose 0.94 (head last) and 1.09 (head on the host) ms per ms of added RTT, one worker; the registered prediction was 2. Re-pricing those cells with one trip (exploratory, post hoc) moved the +10 ms cells from +9.0 / +9.2 % to -1.6 / -0.8 %.
evidence.caveat: at gigabit the second trip had been absorbing real per-visit overhead: the 2026-10-09 pilot's pooled placements measured 4.3-4.4 % slower than the 2-trip predictions, and RTT1 makes them about 1 % more optimistic. RTT1 corrects the round-trip COEFFICIENT; a per-visit overhead term is a separate question, measured (exploratory) by the same study at its unshaped setting.

test.study: the ring-lap study (testbed/dataset/ring_laps_predictions_20261009.json, registered after this file): TinyLlama with the Pi 4 holding 4 blocks and the Jetson 18, in 1, 2, 3 and 4 laps (1-4 Jetson visits per token), unshaped and with +5 ms RTT (netshape.sh, the Pi 4 <-> Jetson path only).
test.statistic: c = the slope, through the origin, of [decode ms/token at +5 ms - unshaped] over the number of Jetson visits k = 1..4, divided by the RTT increase measured by ping in the same round; the mean over rounds.
test.decision: c in [0.75, 1.25]: RTT1 holds and is adopted (new registrations pass rtt_trips=1; the default stays 2 for reproducibility). c in [1.75, 2.25]: the 2-trip model stands. Otherwise neither holds, and both are reported.
